root.text:
Voilà! In view, a vagabond veteran, vested in violet, victim of a vessel of vicissitude that has vanished — and vowing, at last, to vindicate the vexed and the vanquished and the very nearly—

... Sorry. Sorry.

You get a V and it takes the whole night off you. It's the most generous letter in the alphabet and it has no self-control whatsoever and neither have I when I'm holding one.

Right. What can I do for you, chef.

options.text: "Things float in this kitchen when you talk."
Say nothing at all and watch him work.

check.success_text:
Eleven minutes of silence and a man doing prep, and in eleven minutes he does not once look at what his hands are doing.

He is watching the door. Not the pass, not the pans, the *door*, continuously, the whole shift, and he has arranged his entire station so that he can do that without it being visible that he is doing it.
check.failure_text:
He preps.

It is soothing and extremely fast and entirely opaque — the hands go where they go, the knife does what it does, and there is no visible relationship between the attention he is paying and the work getting done.

At the end of eleven minutes there is a great deal of prepared food and you have learned nothing at all except that he is very good at this, which everybody in this parish already knew.

clue.title: He watches the door
clue.text: "T" has arranged his whole station so he can watch the door for an entire shift without anybody noticing that he is.

options.text: Let him get back to the pass.

why_t.text:
Because it's the first letter of the thing I'm not going to tell you, and because Chef couldn't say the rest of it, and because when she said the first letter it came out *perfectly*.

One clean consonant. No air in it, no whistle, nothing to trip over. She said T and it was the only sound in eleven years that came out of that woman exactly as it went in, and I have been called T from that afternoon and I will be called T at the end.

That's not a sad story either. That's the best thing anybody ever did for me and she did it by accident, standing at a stove, not looking up.

options.text: "Then take the letter apart. What is a T."

check.success_text:
"Ha! Right. Right — nobody has ever asked me that and I have had eleven years to get ready for it."

He puts the knife down, which he does not do.

"*Taw.* That's the Phoenician. Last letter of the alphabet, and it means a mark — the mark you make when you cannot write, the one you put at the bottom of a thing to say you were there and you agreed to it. A cross. A signature for a man with no letters.

So I'm the mark at the end. That's the etymology and I'd be lying if I said I hadn't looked it up, and I'd be lying twice if I said I looked it up recently."

A beat. The extraction fan has gone quiet again.

"Man with no name signs with a T. It's not the worst arrangement anybody in this parish has come to."
check.failure_text:
"Tee. As in the letter, as in the drink, as in the thing you hit a ball off."

He shrugs, cheerfully, entirely unbothered, and picks the knife back up.

"I do the sound, chef. That's the job and it's the whole job. I've never once done the history and I'd probably be worse at the sound if I had."

clue.title: The mark a man makes who cannot write
clue.text: T knows his own etymology: taw, the last Phoenician letter, meaning the mark made by someone who cannot write — the cross at the foot of a document to say you were there and agreed. A man with no name signs with a T.

rest_of_it.text:
He opens his mouth.

And then he stands there with it open for about four seconds, in whites, with a knife in his hand, and the extraction fan has gone quiet again the way it does, and there is a ladle on the pass that is not touching the pass.

"...Huh," he says.

He puts the knife down. He tries again. Nothing arrives. He is not being coy — you have watched a man reach for his own name and come back with his hand empty, twice, and the second time he laughed, which was worse.

"Well," he says. "That's new."

clue.title: There is no rest of it
clue.text: Asked for the rest of his name, T reaches for it twice and comes back with nothing. He is not being coy. It is not there.

sorry.text:
No — no, don't. Don't do that.

I've had a name-shaped hole in me for eleven years and I've been walking around it in the dark and calling it modesty. You put a light on. That's a service. In this trade we charge for that.

And besides — he picks the knife back up, and the fan comes back on, and the ladle settles — besides, a man with one letter has got one letter to *be excellent at*, and I have been, and there is not a soul in this parish who does a T like I do a T.

utensils.text:
They do. Not always. Not on request, before you ask, and everybody asks, and I've stopped being wounded by it.

It's the long ones. When a sentence runs — when it's *going*, when the sound has got hold of the thing and the thing has stopped being a list of words and started being a shape — that's when the pass goes light. Ladles. A whisk once, quite high. Chef's second knife, which frightened everybody including the knife.

And it stops the second I stop. Never a moment after. It doesn't fall, either — it *settles*, like it's been put down by somebody who wasn't finished.

passive.text:
It stops the second he stops. Not a moment after — *the second*, on the syllable — and nothing falls.

That is the whole finding and it will not be improved by watching it again. Whatever is holding those objects up is not losing its grip when he finishes the sentence. It is putting them down, deliberately, at the correct height, in the order it picked them up.

It was listening.

He has told this to people before and been laughed at.

You can hear where the laughter landed — there is a small hard shell built around the telling of it now, a slight flattening of the delivery, a pre-emptive shrug in the middle where the interesting part should be.

And he is telling you anyway, with the shell on, because it is true and because you asked.

clue.title: It settles, rather than falls
clue.text: Utensils rise during T's longest sentences and never fall when he stops — they settle, as though put down by somebody who was not finished.

options.text: Do not ask him. Ask the ladle.

check.success_text:
The ladle is on the pass and it is not quite touching the pass, and it has been in that condition for the length of a sentence about tureens.

So: what does the ladle want.

The answer arrives fully dressed and entirely unembarrassed, the way they do, and it is this — the ladle does not want anything. The ladle is *being held*, gently, at the height at which a person holds a thing they intend to give back, by something that has been in this kitchen a very long time and has never once been thanked for the catching.

And it likes the long sentences. It likes them the way a dog likes a particular voice, without understanding one word.
check.failure_text:
The ladle is a ladle.

It is a ladle nine inches above a steel counter, and it is entirely uninterested in being interviewed, and it has the specific inertness of an object that has been asked a question by somebody who did not have the standing to ask it.

After a while T says, kindly, without turning round, "It doesn't do requests," and goes back to the prep.

clue.title: Being held, not lifted
clue.text: The utensils over T's pass are not rising. They are being held at giving-back height by something long resident in the kitchen that has never been thanked, and that likes the sound of the long sentences without understanding them.

speech.text:
You want the T one.

Nobody wants the T one. They want the V one, because they've heard the V one, because the V one travels — somebody does it in a pub and it comes back to me improved.

Right. Right.

Stand back. Mind the pass — I mean that, actually mind it, stand where you are and not a foot closer. And don't laugh in the middle. Laugh at the end. The middle's load-bearing and a laugh in the middle takes the whole thing down.

the_speech.text:
"Take this," he says, and takes it — a tureen, two hands, both wrists, up to the light.

"Take this tepid, tremulous, thoroughly traduced tureen, this trifling triumph of the tuber, tended these three thousand tedious turns of the tap by a toothless titan who tastes nothing and therefore tastes *truly* — and tell me, tell me truthfully, that the tongue is the arbiter of the table.

It is not. It is a tenant. It is a tenant of a house it did not build and pays no rent on, and it holds forth about the furniture.

What you are tasting is not the thing. What you are tasting is the *telling* of the thing — the sequence, the timing, the terrible patience of a woman who has not tasted since 1971 and has not been wrong since 1974 — and if you can taste that, then the tongue is a courtesy, and the truth of a dish is in how it has been *told*."

And there are four utensils in the air over the pass, and a colander, and a small pan.

He stops.

They settle, one after another, at intervals — the way a person puts things down when they have been listening and are going back to work.

clue.title: The telling of the thing
clue.text: T's soliloquy, delivered to six floating utensils: what you taste is not the thing but the telling of it. They settle one after another, at intervals, when he stops.

options.text: Laugh. At the end, as instructed.

after.text:
HA! Yes. Yes — thank you, at the *end*, do you see, that's how it's done, and there are people in this parish who have been coming here for a decade and cannot manage it.

He is genuinely, uncomplicatedly delighted, in whites, with a tureen, in a kitchen where six things have just come down out of the air.

after_quiet.text:
Nothing.

He waits, in whites, holding a tureen, for about three seconds longer than anybody should have to.

Then he puts it down and says, in an ordinary voice: "Right," and turns back to the pass, and the extraction fan comes on, and by the door there is a patch of air about a yard across that has gone thick, and it is in this kitchen and not in Woolbinkle's, and it has never been in this kitchen before.

clue.title: A thickened patch, in the wrong building
clue.text: A failed response to T leaves a yard-wide patch of thickened air in the Lishush Mush kitchen — the same phenomenon as Cheeses Thrice, in a building where it has never happened before.

the_ladle.text:
"You went quiet," says T, without turning round. "People go quiet at the pass sometimes. I've stopped asking."

He sets the ladle down properly, in its place, and it goes where he puts it and stays there like any other object in the world.

"For what it's worth — and I've never said this because it sounds like a man taking credit for weather — I don't think they come up for the sound. I think they come up for the *effort*. Long sentence, nobody listening, four hundred covers, and up they go.

Something in this kitchen likes it when a man tries too hard. That's the whole of my theology and it has served me well."

letter_t.text:
"Right. Enough of that, I've got a hundred and ten covers and a woman out there who cannot say her own consonants and does not care.

But — thank you. Genuinely. Not for the etymology. For asking a question about me that had an answer in it.

Most people ask what the T stands for. You asked what a T *is*. That's a different question and it's the one I could actually do."
